rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese term for a sensational or less serious tabloid newspaper.

example.english: This tabloid is always using huge headlines to report celebrity gossip.
example.traditional: 呢份小報成日用大字標題講明星緋聞。
example.jyutping: ni1 fan6 siu2 bou3 seng4 jat6 jung6 daai6 zi6 biu1 tai4 gong2 ming4 sing1 fei1 man4

rows.note: This is the all-purpose colloquial choice for gossip-oriented, attention-seeking journalism.

example.english: This tabloid news only knows how to sensationalize celebrities' private lives.
example.traditional: 呢啲八卦新聞淨係識得炒作明星私生活。
example.jyutping: ni1 di1 baat3 gwaa3 san1 man4 zing6 hai6 sik1 dak1 caau2 zok3 ming4 sing1 si1 sang1 wut6

rows.note: Use this when the tabloid style mainly relies on emotional or sensational presentation.

example.english: This tabloid report is so emotional that it brings tears to your eyes.
example.traditional: 呢篇報道寫得太煽情，睇到人眼濕濕。
example.jyutping: ne1 pin1 bou3 dou6 se2 dak1 taai3 sin3 cing4 tai2 dou3 jan4 ngaan5 sap1 sap1

rows.note: Use this when explicitly describing something as having the style associated with a tabloid newspaper.

example.english: The paper covered the accident in a tabloid manner.
example.traditional: 該報以小報式手法處理事故報道。
example.jyutping: goi1 bou3 ji5 siu2 bou3 sik1 sau2 faat3 cyu2 lei5 si6 gu3 bou3 dou6
